Protein
The current RDA for protein (0.8 g/kg/day) is the same for adults of all ages, although 
there is evidence that a higher protein intake could help counteract sarcopenia (loss 
of muscle mass) by enhancing hypertrophic response to strength conditioning in the 
older adult.14 The oldest age groups are most at risk for protein deficiency, especially 
when health problems or other stresses are manifested and when patients are institu-
tionalized, hospitalized, or reside in long-term care facilties.
Lipids, Carbohydrates, and Fiber
There is a decrease in the intake of fat and cholesterol with age. There is also a reduction 
in the percentage of calories coming from fat. While absolute intake of carbohydrate 
typically decreases with age, carbohydrate as a percentage of calories increases slightly
